mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level compresses equity valuations by increasing discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% over the past 3 months signals a strengthening labor market that supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when UNRATE < 4.0% is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising industrial production (INDPRO) and falling unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a robust economic expansion that supports equity returns, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days when INDPRO rises by at least 0.5% and UNRATE falls by at least 0.2% over the past 3 months.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises >=0.5% and UNRATE falls >=0.2% in 3 months
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when INDPRO rises >=0.5% and UNRATE falls >=0.2% is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1400 thousand units for 3 consecutive months, it signals a strong housing market that supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return when HOUST > 1400 is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained annual inflation rate above 3.0% (CPIAUCSL) compresses real equity valuations by increasing the real discount rate, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day forward return when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annually is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher residential sales figure (RSAFS) level is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as it signals a strong economy and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 112 for 3 consecutive months, it signals a robust manufacturing sector that supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return when INDPRO > 112 is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annually), the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to increased risk aversion and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annually is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
